exposure: Use of fetal pillow device during cesarean delivery
outcome: Intraoperative complications (uterine incision extension, need for breech extraction)
Requirement for return to hospital or operating theatre
Requirement for neonatal intensive care admission
cohort: 174 women who underwent fully dilated cesarean deliveries at Ipswich Hospital, Australia, between January 2014 and December 2018
finding: While the use of a fetal pillow device during cesarean delivery did not significantly reduce operative complications, it was associated with a decreased length of hospital stay and higher neonatal arterial pH at delivery.
